Specific MacOS Commands

Use sw_vers for the macOS release and build.[2] Query hardware values with sysctl and memory-page statistics with vm_stat instead of the Linux-only /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/meminfo, and free commands.[3][4]

#System info
date
cal
uptime #show time from starting
w #list users
whoami #this <USERNAME>
finger <USERNAME> #info about <USERNAME>
uname -a #Darwin kernel information
sw_vers #macOS version and build
sysctl -n hw.model #Hardware model identifier
sysctl -n hw.memsize #Physical memory in bytes
vm_stat #Memory statistics in pages
df #check disk

launchctl list #List services
atq #List "at" tasks for the <USERNAME>
sysctl -a #List kernel configuration
diskutil list #List connected hard drives
nettop #Monitor network usage of processes in top style

system_profiler SPSoftwareDataType #System info
system_profiler SPPrintersDataType #Printer
system_profiler SPApplicationsDataType #Installed Apps
system_profiler SPFrameworksDataType #Installed framework
system_profiler SPDeveloperToolsDataType #Developer tools info
system_profiler SPStartupItemDataType #Startup Items
system_profiler SPNetworkDataType #Network Capabilities
system_profiler SPFirewallDataType #Firewall Status
system_profiler SPNetworkLocationDataType #Known Network
system_profiler SPBluetoothDataType #Bluetooth Info
system_profiler SPEthernetDataType #Ethernet Info
system_profiler SPUSBDataType #USB info
system_profiler SPAirPortDataType #Airport Info


#Searches
mdfind <PASSWORD> #Show all the files that contains the word <PASSWORD>
mdfind -name <PASSWORD> #Search indexed file names for <PASSWORD>


#Open any app
open -a <Application Name> --hide #Open app hidden
open some.doc -a TextEdit #Open a file in one application


#Computer doesn't go to sleep
caffeinate &


#Screenshot
# May prompt for Screen Recording permission; -x does not bypass it
screencapture -x /tmp/ss.png #Save screenshot; -x only suppresses the sound


#Get clipboard info
pbpaste


#system_profiler
system_profiler --help #This command without arguments take lot of memory and time.
system_profiler -listDataTypes
system_profiler SPSoftwareDataType SPNetworkDataType


#Network
arp -i en0 -l -a #Print the macOS device's ARP table
lsof -i -P -n | grep LISTEN
smbutil statshares -a #View smb shares mounted to the hard drive

#networksetup - set or view network options: Proxies, FW options and more
networksetup -listallnetworkservices #List network services
networksetup -listallhardwareports #Hardware ports
networksetup -getinfo Wi-Fi #Wi-Fi info
networksetup -getautoproxyurl Wi-Fi #Get proxy URL for Wifi
networksetup -getwebproxy Wi-Fi #Wifi Web proxy
networksetup -getftpproxy Wi-Fi #Wifi ftp proxy
scutil --proxy #Current system proxy configuration
scutil --dns #Current DNS resolver configuration
scutil --nc list #Configured VPN services


#Brew
brew list #List installed
brew search <text> #Search package
brew info <formula>
brew install <formula>
brew uninstall <formula>
brew cleanup #Remove older versions of installed formulae.
brew cleanup <formula> #Remove older versions of specified formula.


#Make the machine talk
say hello -v diego
#spanish: diego, Jorge, Monica
#mexican: Juan, Paulina
#french: Thomas, Amelie

########### High privileges actions
sudo purge #purge RAM
#Sharing preferences
sudo launchctl load -w /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/ssh.plist (enable ssh)
sudo launchctl unload /System/Library/LaunchDaemons/ssh.plist (disable ssh)
#Start apache
sudo apachectl (start|status|restart|stop)
 ##Web folder: /Library/WebServer/Documents/
#Remove DNS cache
dscacheutil -flushcache
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder

mdfind queries the Spotlight metadata index, so a missing result does not prove a file is absent.[5] For a filesystem search of accessible paths, use find "$HOME" -iname '*password*' 2>/dev/null.[11] TCC-protected directories can still be unavailable to the calling process.[9]

For network reconnaissance, compare a service's stored proxy settings from networksetup with the current proxy, DNS, and VPN state from scutil.[6][12] A VPN can push a proxy configuration that is visible through scutil --proxy.[13] A network extension can filter traffic without appearing as a conventional proxy.[10] See macOS defensive tooling before assuming direct egress is available.

Screen capture from an SSH session

A remote shell is not automatically in the logged-in user's GUI bootstrap. If you have the required privilege and an active GUI session, identify the correct loginwindow PID for that session and run screencapture in its bootstrap with launchctl bsexec.[7] This adopts the Mach bootstrap and audit-session context, not the process UID or TCC Screen Recording grant.[8] A capture can still be denied or prompt for consent; see screen-capture permissions.[9]

pgrep -fl loginwindow # Identify the loginwindow PID for the target GUI session
LOGINWINDOW_PID=1234 # Replace with that PID
sudo launchctl bsexec "$LOGINWINDOW_PID" /usr/sbin/screencapture -x /tmp/ss.png

Quick anti-analysis / virtualization check

Some macOS stealers call system_profiler to detect VMs and abort with a distinct exit code (e.g., 100) to avoid sandbox detonation[1]:

if system_profiler SPHardwareDataType SPDisplaysDataType | grep -Eiq 'qemu|kvm|vmware|virtualbox'; then
  exit 100
fi

Installed Software & Services

Check for suspicious applications installed and privileges over the.installed resources:

system_profiler SPApplicationsDataType #Installed Apps
system_profiler SPFrameworksDataType #Installed framework
lsappinfo list #Installed Apps
launchctl list #Services

User Processes

# will print all the running services under that particular <USERNAME> domain.
launchctl print gui/<users UID>

# will print all the running services under root
launchctl print system

# will print detailed information about the specific launch agent. And if it’s not running or you’ve mistyped, you will get some output with a non-zero exit code: Could not find service “com.company.launchagent.label” in <DOMAIN> for login
launchctl print gui/<user's UID>/com.company.launchagent.label
